newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Diesel to acquire Outboard Marine.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Diesel to acquire Outboard Marine.

text.p: Detroit Diesel Corp reached a definitive agreement to acquire Outboard Marine Corp in a two-step cash and stock transaction valued at about $500 million, Detroit Diesel said Wednesday.
Detroit Diesel said it will shortly begin a two-step transaction to acquire the outstanding common shares of Outboard, based in Waukegan, Ill., for $16 per share.
The first step will be a cash tender offer for about 67 percent on a fully diluted basis of outstanding Outboard shares, Detroit Diesel said.

The second step two will be to purchase the remaining Outboard shares for a combination of cash and four million shares of Detroit Diesel common stock, said the company, which is a wholly owned unit of Penske Corp, a closely held group of transport companies.
"The aggregate value of the transaction is approximately $500 million, including the assumption of OMC's existing debt of approximately $180 million," Detroit Diesel said.
In addition to the equity offering, the acquisition will be financed through a new credit facility, the company said.

The agreement, subject to customary conditions, provides for merger of a new Detroit Diesel unit with Outboard, the largest U.S. manufacturer of outboard marine engines and the second-largest maker of recreational powerboats.
The board of directors of Outboard has approved the offer and the merger, Detroit Diesel said.
"Our objective is to further expand our worldwide marine capabilities beyond diesel engines with the OMC enterprises," said Detroit Diesel chairman Roger Penske.

"In addition, we look forward to the prospect of further developing OMC's proprietary FICHT fuel injection technology to optimize the performance, fuel economy and emissions capability for the next generation of marine and other engines," Penske said.
Outboard chairman Harry Bowman said, "We believe this offer maximizes value for our current owners."
Combined net revenues for Detroit Diesel and Outboard in 1996 would have been $3.2 billion, the company said.
Outboard products include Johnson and Evinrude engines, and Chris-Craft, Grumman, Four Winns and Stratos powerboats.

Detroit Diesel makes heavy-duty diesel and other engines for trucks, buses, power generation, cars, boats, military vehicles and construction, mining and industrial equipment. The Penske group has annual revenues exceeding $6 billion, Detroit Diesel said.
